title: Roos realization with prescribed quotient-linear reductions
statement:
Fix the finite-field coefficient datum of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], with characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Let $W$ be a scheme with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $B_n=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_W$ for $n\geq1$ and $R=\lim_n B_n$. Write $\operatorname{red}_n=-\otimes_R^L B_n$ and $\operatorname{Res}_n$ for derived extension and restriction of scalars along $R\to B_n$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction, def-weil-integral-derived-restriction-of-scalars], and use the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $P\in D(R)$ be derived complete in the Roos-triangle sense [def-weil-derived-complete]. Let $\mathcal S_\bullet$ be its strict reduction tower [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], with finite-level evaluations identified with objects $S_n\in D(B_n)$ by specified quotient-compatible isomorphisms $b^S_n:\operatorname{red}_nP\xrightarrow{\sim}S_n$. Set $c^S_n=\operatorname{Res}_n(b^S_n)\circ\eta_{n,P}$, where $\eta_{n,P}:P\to\operatorname{Res}_n\operatorname{red}_nP$ is the scalar-extension unit of [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction]. Let $\mathcal T_\bullet$ be a normalized DVR tower with finite-level objects $T_n$ [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower], and let $G:\mathcal S_\bullet\to\mathcal T_\bullet$ be a morphism in the derived category of strict $R$-module towers whose evaluation is $\operatorname{Res}_n(g_n)$ for specified isomorphisms $g_n:S_n\xrightarrow{\sim}T_n$. Use the total derived inverse-limit functor with its natural Roos triangles and projections [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit, def-weil-derived-limit, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], and put $L_S=R\lim\mathcal S_\bullet$ and $L_T=R\lim\mathcal T_\bullet$.

There exists an isomorphism $e:P\xrightarrow{\sim}L_S$ satisfying $p^S_n\circ e=c^S_n$ for every $n$, and $F=R\lim G:L_S\to L_T$ is an isomorphism. For $\gamma=F\circ e$, the scalar-extension adjoints $b^T_n:\operatorname{red}_n L_T\to T_n$ of the actual projections $p^T_n$ are isomorphisms, compatible with all quotient normalizations, and
$$p^T_n\circ\gamma=\operatorname{Res}_n(g_n)\circ c^S_n,\qquad b^T_n\circ\operatorname{red}_n(\gamma)=g_n\circ b^S_n.$$ The projection equality is in $D(R)$; the reduction equality is in $D(B_n)$.
No uniqueness of $e$ or $G$ is asserted. No boundedness, constructibility, or common integral local model is assumed.

proof.text: Derived completeness supplies a K-flat resolution q:K→H, an identification QH≅P, and an augmented reduction Roos triangle. Put eK=Q(q) followed by this identification. The universal scalar-extension counit is invertible on K. Its exact-restriction comparison gives a_n:Res_n(red_n P)≅Q(integralTowerComplex_n K). The normalized derived adjunction identifies unit_n followed by a_n with eK.inv followed by the localized tensor unit: this follows from the counit compatibility in the recorded adjunction and the pure-tensor characterization of integralTowerUnit. The declared K-flat transition theorem identifies the adjacent transitions under a_n. Conjugating by Siso_n and Res_n(bS_n.inv) therefore gives a levelwise isomorphism from the evaluated S tower to the integral reduction tower. Product extensionality conjugates 1-s; transport the distinguished completeness triangle through the product isomorphism. Its first arrow has components c_n=unit_n followed by Res_n(bS_n.hom) followed by Siso_n.inv.

source.place: Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit; TR1 invariance under isomorphism; applied to the completeness triangle specified in def-weil-derived-complete

proof.text: Compare the triangle from Step 1 with the specified Roos triangle of $L_S$. Rotate both once so that $1-s_S:A_S\to A_S$ is the first arrow. The identity maps on these two terms commute with that arrow. TR3 supplies the third component; rotate back to obtain a triangle morphism $(e,1_{A_S},1_{A_S})$ with $e:P\to L_S$. Both $P$ and $L_S$ are derived limits of the same system and the evaluated tower map is the identity. The Roos-triangle isomorphism criterion makes $e$ an isomorphism. The first square says $\iota_S e=c^S$, hence $p^S_n e=c^S_n$ after the $n$th product projection. TR3 gives existence, with no uniqueness claim.

source.place: Tag 08TC, paragraph following definition-derived-limit (TR3 comparison); Tag 014A, lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle

proof.text: The equation hG identifies every evaluation of G with a composite of the specified isomorphisms Siso_n, Res_n(g_n), and T.evaluationIso_n.inv, so each evaluation is invertible. Exact evaluation on strict towers commutes with derived homology (Mathlib Functor.mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso). Hence every component of every homology map of G is invertible. A natural transformation with invertible components is invertible; DerivedCategory.isIso_iff then gives IsIso G. Any functor preserves isomorphisms, so RF.map G is invertible. Use the assumed projection naturality, project with Pi.π_n and substitute hG and the projection equation of Step 2. This gives the asserted projection identity for gamma=e.hom followed by RF.map G. No naturality of the connecting maps is needed.

source.place: Cohomology detects isomorphisms in a derived category; exact evaluation commutes with cohomology. Implemented with Mathlib DerivedCategory.isIso_iff and Functor.mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso. Projection naturality is an explicit unchanged hypothesis.

proof.text: Let $b^T_n:\operatorname{red}_nL_T\to T_n$ be the adjoint of $p^T_n$ under $\operatorname{red}_n\dashv\operatorname{Res}_n$. By naturality of this Hom bijection in its source, the adjoint of $p^T_n\gamma$ is $b^T_n\operatorname{red}_n(\gamma)$. By naturality in its target and the unit formula, the adjoint of $\operatorname{Res}_n(g_n)c^S_n=\operatorname{Res}_n(g_nb^S_n)\eta_{n,P}$ is $g_nb^S_n$. Applying the bijection to Step 3 thus proves $b^T_n\operatorname{red}_n(\gamma)=g_nb^S_n$ in $D(B_n)$. In particular $b^T_n=(g_nb^S_n)\operatorname{red}_n(\gamma)^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. This proves quotient-linearity directly in the target-ring derived category; it does not infer equality there from faithfulness of restriction.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint, bifunctorial Hom bijection and unit for identity underlying topoi

proof.text: First derive the adjacent cone equation from p followed by (1-s)=0 in the distinguished Roos triangle, by composing with a product projection. Induct on n≤m, using composition and identity of the localized evaluation transformations, to obtain p_m followed by the evaluated transition m→n equals p_n for every quotient. The tower_tau equation identifies that transition with Res_m(T.tau) and the canonical restriction-composition isomorphism. Apply the completed scalar adjunction at m to the claimed equation reduction_m followed by T.tau = quotientUnit followed by Res_(m,n)(reduction_n). Naturality in the target identifies its left transpose with p_m followed by the restricted tau. By the definition of quotientUnit as the transpose of unit_n followed by the inverse restriction-composition isomorphism, naturality of that isomorphism and the unit formula identify the right transpose with p_n. The cone equation equates them; injectivity of the Hom equivalence proves the result. This works also for m=n and does not use a separate scalar-associator theorem or faithfulness of restriction.
